name: Burn word-highlighted karaoke captions onto a video with FFmpeg

parameters.content:
## Burn word-highlighted karaoke captions onto any video with FFmpeg (free, no API)

Upload a video that already has narration in it - your own voiceover, a downloaded clip, output from another tool - plus the script of what's said, and get back the same video with word-by-word highlighted captions burned in. No API key, no account, no paid service: FFmpeg's ASS subtitle renderer does the real work, running for free on your own machine.

This is a standalone captioning step, distinct from this creator's other karaoke template (that one only outputs a subtitle file and MP3 - it never touches video). This one burns captions straight into picture for any video you already have, regardless of how the narration was recorded.

**Customization built in:** pick from 4 caption styles - classic bottom captions, a bold high-contrast highlight style for punchy shorts, top-of-frame placement for videos that already have something important at the bottom (like a UI demo or a face-cam), or plain burned-in lines with no per-word highlight at all - a genuinely different render path for anyone who wants standard subtitles instead of karaoke.

### How it works

1. A form takes a video file, the exact script spoken in it, and a caption style.
2. The video is saved to a per-run temp folder and its real duration and resolution are read with FFprobe.
3. The script's words are distributed across that duration by character length (an estimate - there's no per-word timing signal for arbitrary narration), then grouped into readable lines. For the 3 karaoke styles, each line is written with per-word `\k` timing tags; for Plain burned-in, the same lines are written as static text with no timing tags at all. Either way the ASS file is sized to the video's own resolution, using the colors/weight/position of the chosen style.
4. FFmpeg burns that subtitle file directly into the video and the result is read back off disk.

### Setup

Self-hosted n8n only - this uses Execute Command, which n8n Cloud disables. Install FFmpeg **with libass support** on the PATH of the process running n8n (plain `brew install ffmpeg` on macOS does NOT include libass - use `brew install ffmpeg-full` instead, or check with `ffmpeg -filters | grep subtitles`). Start n8n with `NODES_EXCLUDE="[]"` and `N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO="/tmp"`.

## 1. Upload
A video with narration already in it, the exact script, and a caption style (classic / bold highlight / top / plain burned-in).

## 2. Measure
FFprobe reads the video's real duration and resolution.

## 3. Build captions
Words are timed by character length and written as a karaoke .ass file.

## 4. Burn + deliver
FFmpeg renders the captions into the picture, then the result is read back.

## Self-hosted only + needs libass
Execute Command needs self-hosted n8n. See Setup - plain Homebrew ffmpeg lacks libass.

parameters.formDescription: Upload a video that already has narration in it, paste the script, and pick a caption style. You get back the same video with the captions burned in - word-highlighted karaoke, or plain static lines.

nodes.name: Prepare Run
nodes.notes: Builds a per-run temp folder, detects the uploaded video's binary property name, and splits the caption text into words.

nodes.name: Create the temp folder
nodes.notes: mkdir -p is safe to run again. This wipes json + binary, restored in the next node.

nodes.name: Restore the uploaded video
nodes.notes: Execute Command replaces the item with its own stdout/stderr/exitCode - re-attach the video's binary and the paths from Prepare Run.

nodes.name: Save the video to disk
nodes.notes: Writes the uploaded video to the temp folder so FFprobe/FFmpeg (Execute Command) can read it by path.

nodes.name: Read video duration and resolution (FFprobe)
nodes.notes: Reads the video's real duration and resolution - the only timing/sizing signal available for arbitrary narration. Reads the path from Prepare Run, not $json.

nodes.name: Build the karaoke captions (.ass)
nodes.notes: Distributes words across the measured duration by character length, groups them into readable lines, and writes a karaoke-tagged (\k) ASS subtitle file sized to the video's own resolution.

nodes.name: Save the captions file to disk
nodes.notes: Writes the generated .ass subtitle file so FFmpeg's subtitles filter can read it by path.

nodes.name: Burn the captions into the video (FFmpeg)
nodes.notes: Requires an FFmpeg build with libass. Video is re-encoded (captions are burned into pixels); audio is stream-copied unchanged.

nodes.name: Verify the burn succeeded
nodes.notes: Throws with the real FFmpeg error if the exit code was not 0 - the most common cause is an FFmpeg build without libass.

nodes.name: Read the captioned video back
nodes.notes: Reads the finished MP4 off disk as binary output - the free-path deliverable, no external service involved.

nodes.name: Attach the caption report to the file
nodes.notes: Read/Write File's read operation replaces json with file metadata only - merges the word/line/duration report back in so the output has both the summary and the file.
